feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible — single-column ELM cannot represent basin-scale lateral groundwater flow, well pumping, or aquifer recovery; those require a distributed/3D groundwater model. ELM can quantify the surface-water-budget drivers (recharge, ET, drainage) that feed the aquifer, and PFLOTRAN can be coupled to simulate saturated-zone response to a pumping change at column scale, but a true 'basin recovery over a decade' evaluation is outside single-column ELM's scope.
answerable: Local vertical recharge flux to the water table under representative land-cover/soil conditions in the Upper Iowa basin
ELM-simulated water-table depth (ZWT), drainage (QDRAI), and ET partitioning at point/column scale over a decade
PFLOTRAN column-scale saturated-zone head response to a prescribed 30% reduction in extraction (as a boundary sink term)
Sensitivity of soil moisture and recharge to interannual climate variability over the 10-year window
not_answerable: Basin-integrated aquifer water-level recovery, which requires lateral 3D groundwater flow and regional boundary conditions not represented in single-column configuration
Explicit agricultural pumping wells and their spatial drawdown cones (ELM has no pumping/irrigation-well demand routing to a confined aquifer)
Stream-aquifer exchange and baseflow recovery across the drainage network
Well-by-well or subregional allocation impacts of the 30% policy

parsed.n_justification: Three columns span the dominant land-cover/soil gradient of the Upper Iowa basin: intensive row-crop uplands on silty clay loam, riparian/alluvial lowland near the river with a shallow water table, and a mixed grass/pasture terrace. This brackets the recharge and water-table behavior relevant to evaluating pumping-reduction effects without implying a spatially resolved basin simulation.
requires_capabilities: PFLOTRAN coupling for saturated-zone flow with a prescribed extraction sink term to emulate a 30% pumping reduction
STOP_OPTION set to nyears for a decadal run
Multi-year atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 or site-adjusted CLM-NCEP) covering 2005-2014
Crop/managed-vegetation module for realistic row-crop ET and rooting in the upland column
assumptions: The 30% pumping reduction is represented in PFLOTRAN as a proportional decrease in a subsurface sink term, since single-column ELM has no explicit agricultural well demand
Basin-scale recovery is approximated only through column-scale recharge and head response; lateral flow and stream-aquifer exchange are neglected
Soil textures assigned from SSURGO/gridded surrogates typical of Upper Iowa basin land units
A 10-year forcing window (2005-2014) is used as a representative decade of climate variability; a longer spinup is applied before the analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and water table
Land cover is held fixed over the decade so simulated differences reflect hydrologic response rather than land-use change
